holidays.name: National Magic Day
holidays.description: A day for pulling rabbits out of hats, learning a card trick, and wondering how the magician did it. Magicians and fans mark it with shows, tricks, and a little mystery.
holidays.origin: The day honors Harry Houdini, the famed escape artist and illusionist, who died on October 31, 1926. It was created to celebrate the art of magic and keep his legacy alive.
holidays.funFact: Houdini died on Halloween, 1926. Some people still hold séances every year hoping he will send a message from beyond.

holidays.name: National Knock Knock Joke Day
holidays.description: Today you have an excuse to groan at jokes that start with a knock and end with a terrible pun. Tell a few to friends, family, and trick-or-treaters.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It fits Halloween well, because the holiday is all about people showing up at your door.
holidays.funFact: Knock-knock jokes got hugely popular in the United States in the 1930s, and the format has barely changed since.

holidays.name: National Doorbell Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the humble doorbell, which does more work tonight than on any other day of the year. Ring it with pride, or at least answer it with candy.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It falls on Halloween, when doorbells ring more than at any other time of year.
holidays.funFact: Electric doorbells date back to the 1800s. Before that, visitors announced themselves with knockers or hand-pulled bells.
